Count reads in a batch of FASTA or paired-end FASTQ files

Source: R/vtamR_fun.R
count_reads_batch.Rd

Reads an input information file containing paths to FASTA files or paired-end FASTQ files, counts the sequences in each unique file, and appends the resulting read counts to the information table.

Usage

count_reads_batch(
  info,
  dir,
  outfile = NULL,
  chunk_lines = 1e+05,
  fast_count = TRUE,
  log_file = NULL,
  sep = ","
)

Arguments

info

Character string giving the path to the input information file, or a data frame. The file must contain either a fasta or fastq_fw column.

dir

Character string giving the directory containing the sequence files listed in info.

outfile

Character string giving the path to the output file. If NULL, the information table is not written to disk.

chunk_lines

Integer specifying the maximum number of lines to read at a time when using the chunk-based counting method. Defaults to 1e5. Passed to count_reads().

fast_count

Logical value controlling the counting method. When TRUE on Linux-like systems, shell commands are used for faster counting. When FALSE, the chunk-based R implementation is used. Passed to count_reads().

log_file

Character string specifying the path to the CSV log file. The path is resolved with the following priority:

  1. the log_file argument, if explicitly provided by the user;

  2. the vtamR.log_file option set with options(vtamR.log_file = ...), if set;

  3. "vtamR_log.csv" in the current working directory, used as a last resort if neither of the above is set.

To disable logging entirely, set log_file = NA.

sep

Character string specifying the field separator used to read and write the information file. Defaults to ",".

Value

An updated data frame containing the original information table and a read_count column. For FASTA input, counts are joined using the fasta column. For paired-end FASTQ input, counts are joined using the fastq_fw column. The data frame is returned invisibly.

Details

For FASTA input, the information file must contain a fasta column. For FASTQ input, it must contain fastq_fw column. For paired-end FASTQ files, only the forward-read files in fastq_fw are counted.

The input file paths are interpreted relative to dir. Each unique file is counted once, and the resulting count is joined back to the information table using the corresponding file column.

Each unique sequence file is counted only once, even if it appears multiple times in the information table. The resulting counts are joined back to all matching rows.

The sequence files are expected to be supported by count_reads(), including FASTA and FASTQ files and supported compressed formats.

An error is raised if info does not contain the required sequence-file columns.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Count reads in a FASTA batch
counts <- count_reads_batch(
  info = "fasta_info.csv",
  dir = "data/fasta"
)

# Count reads in paired-end FASTQ files and write the updated table
counts <- count_reads_batch(
  info = "fastq_info.csv",
  dir = "data/fastq",
  outfile = "fastq_info_with_counts.csv",
  sep = ","
)

# Use chunk-based counting
counts <- count_reads_batch(
  info = "fastq_info.csv",
  dir = "data/fastq",
  fast_count = FALSE,
  chunk_lines = 1e5
)
} # }
